semantic_correction.stem: A client who uses a continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion pump reviews infusion-site care with the nurse. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will rotate infusion sites, inspect the skin, and change the infusion set according to my pump's instructions.
options.B: I will keep using the same infusion site until insulin delivery stops because routine site rotation is unnecessary.
options.C: I can skip skin checks because infusion-set sites do not develop infection or other local complications.
options.D: I will use one fixed change interval even when my pump or infusion-set instructions specify a different schedule.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current FDA insulin-pump guidance instructs users to follow pump-specific directions for when to change infusion sets and to rotate infusion sites. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care identify appropriate infusion-site rotation and care as part of proper insulin administration technique and note infusion-set problems, lipohypertrophy, and pump-site infection as recognized complications. Therefore, safe pump use includes site rotation, skin/site assessment, and manufacturer-specific infusion-set replacement rather than a universal interval.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach insulin-pump users to rotate and inspect infusion sites and to change infusion sets according to the specific pump or infusion-set manufacturer's instructions.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor pattern, shortened the correct answer, and preserved FDA's manufacturer-specific infusion-set change instruction plus ADA site-rotation/site-care guidance.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was correct but included an absolute distractor and a longer answer. The revised item tests site rotation, assessment, and device-specific change timing with parallel options.

option_audit.A: Correct. It combines FDA manufacturer-specific change timing with current infusion-site rotation and care recommendations.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Reusing one site increases local complication risk and conflicts with site-rotation guidance.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Pump sites can develop infection, lipohypertrophy, dislodgement, and other local complications.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. FDA directs users to follow pump-specific instructions rather than one universal change interval.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone satisfies both current device-specific replacement guidance and infusion-site care recommendations.
cueing_check: All four choices are client statements about pump-site management of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
